buyer: Aufbau- und Entwicklungsgesellschaft Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler mbH
title: Germany – Construction work – 1H0007, Neubau Feuerwehr Ahrweiler - Los 070 Gebäudeautomation
description: Neubau der Feuerwehr Ahrweiler: Das heutige Gebäude der Freiwilligen Feuerwehr Ahrweiler an der Ramersbacher Straße gegenüber des Ahrtores wurde durch die Flut im Jahr 2021 stark beschädigt. Der verbleibende Torso ist nicht mehr sanierungsfähig, sodass an anderer Stelle ein Ersatzneubau mit 12 Stellplätzen realisiert werden soll. Die neue Lage südlich der Ahr befindet sich in Sichtweite des heutigen Feuerwehrgebäudes. Durch die Umlegung des Feuerwehrgebäudes soll in Zukunft die Erreichbarkeit aller Gebiete auch bei extremen Hochwasser durch die Feuerwehr sichergestellt werden. Im Rahmen von Los 070 wird die Gebäudeautomation ausgeschrieben. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst die Lieferung, Montage und Inbetriebnahme aller Mess-, Steuer- und Regeltechnikkomponenten einschließlich Feldgeräten, Automationsstationen, Netzwerktechnik und Schaltschränken. Zudem sind die vollständige Verkabelung, die Einrichtung der Gebäudeleittechnik, die Programmierung, Prüfungen, Dokumentation sowie die Einweisung des Bedienpersonals auszuführen. Alle Arbeiten erfolgen gemäß VOB/C und den geltenden Normen und Richtlinien, um einen sicheren und zuverlässigen Betrieb der neuen Feuerwache sicherzustellen.

title: Finland – Construction work – SR-urakka, Uudisrakennus, Helsinki, Hermanni, Heka Hermanninranta Albumikatu 3
description: Hankinnan kohteena on asuinkerrostalojen rakentaminen Helsingin Hermanninrantaan SR-urakkana sisältäen kokonaissuunnittelun (mm. ark, rak, lvias, energia, pohjarakennus, elinkaari, akustiikka) ja rakennusteknisten töiden lisäksi kaikki LVIAS- ja pihatyöt. Kokonaisurakkaan lukeutuvat: - Tontit 21685/2 ja 21685/3 (yhdistetään mahdollisesti myöhemmin) Heka Hermanninranta Albumikatu 3 Hankkeen erityispiirteitä: - Kohde koostuu kahdesta erillisestä kerrostalosta ja piha-alueesta, jotka muodostavat puolet korttelikokonaisuudesta. - Kohde voidaan toteuttaa joko puu- tai betonirunkoisena. Betonirunko edellyttää poikkeamispäätöksen hakemista, josta urakoitsija vastaa. - Asuntoala n. 11 040 asm2 ja liiketilan ala n. 55 htm2 lukeutuvat tarjouspyyntöön hankittavaan määrään. - Urakoitsija vastaa kaikesta suunnittelusta. Suunnittelu voidaan aloittaa esisopimuksen allekirjoituksen jälkeen. Rakennustyön arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 04/2028 ja työt tulee aloittaa viimeistään 06/2028. Hankintaa ei jaeta osiin, sillä usean toimittajan malli tuottaisi epätarkoituksenmukaisen sopimuskokonaisuudenaikataulunhallinnan sekä töiden yhteensovittamisen kannalta. Hankinnan kohde on tarkemmin kuvattu tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevissa kaupallisissa ja teknisissä asiakirjoissa. Liiteasiakirjat löytyvät julkaisun Tarjouspalvelu-sivuilta kohdassa "Liitteet ja linkit" ilmoitetusta linkistä.

title: France – Public road transport services – DELEGATION DE SERVICE PUBLIC RELATIVE A LA GESTION ET L’EXPLOITATIONDES SERVICES DE MOBILITE ET DE TRANSPORT DE VOYAGEURS SUR LETERRITOIRE DE CHATEAUROUX METROPOLE
description: La consultation a pour objet de déléguer la gestion et l’exploitation des services de mobilité et de transport de voyageurs sur le ressort territorial de la Communauté d’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole (Réseau Horizon) Châteauroux Métropole, autorité Organisatrice de la mobilité est autorité délégante. Les missions déléguées sont les suivantes: Offre de base : Exploitation et gestion des services de mobilité et de transports publics de personnes et à l’échelle du territoire communautaire selon les principes définis à l’article 5.1 du document programme. Les candidats devront obligatoirement répondre à l’offre de base et à l'option obligatoire.• Option obligatoire :Option N°1 : Exploitation et gestion d’un service de location de vélos L’option est décrite à l’article 5.2 du document programme. L’Autorité Délégante précisera, avant la remise de l'offre finale si l'option est levée. Le Délégataire assurera la gestion de ces services pour une durée de six (6) ans, à compter du 01/01/2028 et jusqu’au 31/12/2033 dans le cadre d’une délégation de service public (DSP) au sein du périmètre contractuel. Lieu d’exécution : Territoire de la Communauté d’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole(département de l’Indre). L’estimation de la valeur du contrat de concession est de 45 millions d’euros HT valeur décembre 2026 sur la durée du contrat. Les missions attendues sont l'organisation, la production et la commercialisation des services, ainsi que la réalisation de l'offre de transport et la maintenance des véhicules et outils de production.Le délégataire assurera en outre la gestion de la relation avec les usagers des transports scolaires qui sont assurés par le biais de marchés publics en cours. La future DSP intègre la gestion et l'exploitation des services de transport suivants sur l’ensemble du périmètre de l’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole : • Le réseau de transport en commun « Horizon » composé aujourd’hui de 12 lignes régulières, • Le service de transport adapté à la demande, « Handibus », à destination des personnes à mobilité réduite sur le périmètre de CM .Pour cette gestion déléguée, la collectivité met à la disposition du délégataire : • Un dépôt de bus réceptionné en 2021 avec une capacité de stationnement de 80 véhicules, équipé de bureaux, d’un atelier de maintenance, de stations de lavage et de carburant et d’équipements de recharge de véhicule électrique; • 31 autobus standard, 5 autobus articulé, 2 midibus. Ces véhicules sont équipés d’équipements de suivi par système SAEIV et cellules de comptage voyageurs. Plusieurs véhicules standard et articulés électriques ont également été commandés. • 2 midibus accessibles et équipés pour accueillir des PMR • Un Site Internet https://www.bushorizon.com/ La présente concession est passée sur le fondement du règlement 1370/2007 et de la directive 2014/23/CEE. La directive 2014/25/UE citée dans le présent avis concerne les marchés des secteurs spéciaux est non les concessions , elle ne s'applique pas à la présente consultation.

title: MP-200051 N13 EP16 Landquart-frontière GR/SG PUN – Laboratoire du maître d’ouvrage
description:
Le projet comprend la réfection complète de la N13 sur le tronçon de près de 6 km entre Landquart et la frontière cantonale GR/SG. En outre, les infrastructures du tronçon entre la jonction de Landquart et l’échangeur de Sarganserland doivent être préparées en vue d’une réaffectation de la bande d’arrêt d’urgence (PUN).

Le mandat mis en soumission porte sur les prestations du laboratoire du maître d’ouvrage pour les phases de réalisation et de mise en service/achèvement.

Le laboratoire du maître d’ouvrage doit contrôler et soumettre à des essais en laboratoire les matériaux et éléments suivants :

- Infrastructures de transport, couches bitumineuses ;

- Terrassements, sols, couches de fondation ;

- Ouvrages en béton ;

- Étanchéités ;

- Dispositifs de retenue des véhicules ;

- Marquages.

title: Unterstützungs- und Programmierleistungen zur Weiterentwicklung von Fachanwendungen
description: Entwicklung, Anpassung, Fehlerbehebung und Test von Fachanwendungen einschließlich technischer Dokumentation Gegenstand der Auftragsvergabe ist der Abschluss eines Rahmenvertrages über Unterstützungsleistungen bei der Weiterentwicklung des integrierten Lagerinformationssystems (ILS) und dem Betriebs-Informations-System (BIS) in Abstimmung mit der technischen Projektleitung der BGZ. description: East Orange, NJ EUL Request for Expressions of Interest DRAFT PRE-DECISIONAL INTERNAL VA USE ONLY 1 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST ENHANCED-USE LEASE DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITY VA New Jersey Healthcare System (VANJHCS) within Veterans Integrated Service Network 2 (VISN 2) East Orange, NJ VA Medical Center (VAMC) located within East Orange, NJ Notice This advertisement is a notice of a potential opportunity. This Request for Expressions of Interest (the advertisement ) is not a solicitation for offers, nor is it a request for proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government assumes no responsibility to award an Enhanced-Use Lease (EUL) based upon responses to this advertisement. This Sources Sought Notice is to identify potential sources for information and planning purposes only and is not intended to pre-qualify or disqualify any potential Respondents. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to conduct market research to determine if there are responsible and qualified entities interested in redeveloping the asset described in Section III and if yes, what potential reuse options exist. The information gained from this Sources Sought will be used to assist the Government in determining if this development opportunity can be competitive and/or a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) Set-Aside. The Government will use this information to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement and to inform related asset management decision-making. The Government requests that interested parties respond to this Notice with the specific information requested in Section V of this Notice and identify their small business status. VA is particularly interested in SDVOSB/VOSB respondents capabilities to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. Developers responding to this market research should be aware that responding to this advertisement may not ensure that they qualify for any underlying future solicitation or contract award. Responding to this Sources Sought Notice is NOT a prerequisite to respond to any future subsequent solicitations. The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this Sources Sought. The Government cannot provide any warranty, expressed or implied, as to the accuracy, reliability or completeness of the information contained in this Notice. Overview and Objectives The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a Developer for purposes of developing administrative and/or educational purposes, or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans (e.g., technical skills / job training centers, research facilities, mixed-use, other). Parking is limited on the campus and if redevelopment would result in significantly increased demand for parking, parking must be included within the footprint. For purposes of this effort, the Developer would be a non-VA entity who has the qualifications outlined in Section V of this Notice. The opportunity would involve a Developer entering into an EUL with VA and financing, renovating/constructing, operating, and maintaining the agreed upon use of the asset. VA s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program. The objective of this development opportunity is to repurpose an asset at the East Orange VAMC Campus under VA s EUL Program to the benefit of Veterans. Respondents should consider the following as they formulate responses to this Notice: Lease-back by VA or other Federal government entities is not permissible, and financing cannot reflect a lease-back arrangement. The PACT Act does not nullify 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(5), which states, "The terms of an enhanced-use lease may not provide for any acquisition, contract, demonstration, exchange, grant, incentive, procurement, sale, other transaction authority, service agreement, use agreement, lease, or lease-back by the Secretary or Federal Government. VA may only receive cash consideration for ground lease rent in an EUL (per 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(B)). This means VA cannot receive any in-kind consideration or free/discounted services as part of a new EUL agreement. However, projects may provide free or discounted services to individual Veterans or Veteran Service Organizations, and the Secretary may enter into an EUL without receiving consideration per U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(C). Additional information on the VA s EUL program may be obtained at: http://www.va.gov/assetmanagement/. Development Scope The intent of this Notice is to determine if there are experienced developers, including SDVOSB or VOSB developers, that can develop the subject Campus asset in accordance with VA s EUL authority. The Developer would undertake all necessary investigation activities to produce development with the underutilized asset at the East Orange Campus. The asset that may be redeveloped by the Developer includes Building 11 (Note: The building is currently listed on the National Register of Historic Places). Please see Attachment A for a map of the Campus and Attachment B for asset information and photos. East Orange VA Medical Center Background The East Orange VA Medical Center located at 385 Tremont Avenue, East Orange, NJ 07018-1023 includes ~34 acres situated on a knoll at South Center Street and Tremont Avenue, 228 feet above sea level. The campus overlooks a residential area with views of the Manhattan skyline on the horizon. The grounds are in four municipalities: Orange, East Orange, South Orange, and Newark. The site formerly belonged to the Bamberger estate, which was endowed originally to Princeton University and in turn, sold to a private owner and then purchased by the government. Recognizing the need for a medical facility to serve Veterans in metropolitan areas, Congress approved and funded the facility in 1943. The VAMC opened in July 1952. The hospital provides primary care and specialty health services, including homeless Veteran care, mental health care, skin care (dermatology), dental care, digestive care (gastroenterology), cardiology, eye health and vision care (ophthalmology and optometry), palliative and hospice care, returning service member care, Veteran readiness and employment programs, and more. Sources Sought Response Requirements VA is seeking qualified developers who have a proven company track record of: Developing projects comparable to the proposed use(s) for the designated asset. Financial wherewithal required to successfully develop the proposed use(s) with associated amenities (if applicable); and, Securing public and private financing for projects comparable to the proposed use(s) for the designated asset. For SDVOSB/VOSB developers, VA is seeking to confirm the Respondent s ability to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. Responses should be submitted on official letterhead, must include a point of contact and the signature of at least one organization officer. Responses must not exceed 15 pages, single spaced with a minimum 12-point font. The information gained from this Sources Sought will be used to assist the Government in determining if this development opportunity can be competitive and/or a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) Set-Aside. Overview and Objectives The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a Developer for purposes of developing a wellness center, supportive housing, or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans (e.g., general affordable housing, skilled nursing facilities, assisted living, technical skills / job training centers, research facilities, mixed-use, other). For purposes of this effort, the Developer would be a non-VA entity who has the qualifications outlined in Section V of this Notice. The opportunity would involve a Developer entering into an EUL with VA and financing, renovating/constructing, operating, and maintaining the agreed upon use of the assets. VA s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program. The objective of this development opportunity is to repurpose assets at the Lyons VAMC Campus under VA s EUL Program to the benefit of Veterans. Respondents should consider the following as they formulate responses to this Notice: Lease-back by VA or other Federal government entities is not permissible, and financing cannot reflect a lease-back arrangement. Lyons VA Medical Center Background The Lyons VA Medical Center was originally designed in the 1920s as a neuropsychiatric hospital capable of treating 400 Veterans. The initial 50 Veterans were admitted as transfers from the Northport, New York VA Hospital on November 12, 1930. Another 50 were transferred from the Bronx VA campus the following day. Located at 151 Knollcroft Road, Lyons, NJ 07939-5001 on ~288 acres, it is part of the VA New Jersey Health Care Network (VISN 2). In 1982, a domiciliary program was established at Lyons to assist Veterans who were homeless to reintegrate into the community after treatment. A 240-bed community living center was completed in 1988. The hospital currently provides primary care and specialty health services, including primary care, skin care (dermatology), dental care, digestive care (gastroenterology), cardiology, geriatrics, optometry, mental health care, hospice and palliative care, women Veteran care, and more. description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes Residential Reentry Center Services located within Sacramento County and other border Counties of San Jaquin, Sutter, Yolo, Solano, Placer, El Dorado, and Amador. Home Confinement within 150 miles of the RRC Facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March 2022�. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. title: Northwest Division Powerhouse Life Safety Upgrades Stage 1
description: Northwest Division Powerhouse Life Safety Upgrades Stage 1The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Walla Walla District, intends to issue a single-phase solicitation on or about 30 November 2026 for a Construction Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple-Award Task Order Contract (MATOC).The anticipated MATOC will provide construction services for renovation and upgrade projects at hydroelectric powerhouses located at large, remote civil works projects within the Northwestern Division. The primary area of performance is anticipated to include USACE Walla Walla District projects at McNary, Ice Harbor, Lower Monumental, Little Goose, Lower Granite, and Dworshak. Task orders may also include work at other USACE projects within the Pacific Northwest, including locations within the Seattle and Portland Districts in Washington, Oregon, Idaho, and Montana.The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Walla Walla District, anticipates awarding up to four (4) IDIQ MATOCs. At least one, and up to two, MATOCs will be reserved for award to qualified small business concerns. Task orders issued under the MATOCs will be firm-fixed-price.The aggregate shared contract capacity for all awarded MATOCs is anticipated to be $99 million. Each contract is anticipated to include a 36-month base period and two (2) 24-month option periods, exercisable at the Governments discretion. The Government may issue individual task orders with values up to $25,000,000.The Government reserves the right to issue additional solicitations and award additional contracts for the same or similar work within the geographic area covered by the MATOCs. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. This notice is for informational purposes only and is not a solicitation. The solicitation is anticipated to be issued on or about 30 November 2026.Summary Scope of Work:The purpose of this IDIQ MATOC is to provide construction services to renovate and upgrade life-safety systems at large hydroelectric powerhouses located at large, remote civil works projects. These powerhouses may range in size from 75,000 square feet to 420,000 square feet and from 5 stories to 11 stories. The work may consist of the following major industrial construction elements for installation and/or modification:1. Fire detection and mass notification alarm systems2. Wet pipe, fine water mist, and clean agent sprinkler fire suppression system(s)3. Smoke control system, including stair pressurization fans, smoke exhaust fans, motorized fire-smoke dampers, and complex logic and programming matrix digital controls4. HVAC direct digital controls5. HVAC ventilation and conditioning equipment, dampers, and ductwork6. Fabricated steel stairs and guardrails7. Architectural fire barrier walls, fire doors, safety glazing and finishes8. Firestopping9. Emergency and exit lighting systems10. Electrical power supply and distribution11. Precast concrete12. Low-slope roofing13. Specific aspects of this project that may be especially challenging include: a. Robust industrial safety protocols with rigorous lockout tagout proceduresb. Construction in a continuously operating industrial environmentc. Proximity to high voltage equipment and transmission linesd. Multiple underground levels with limited accesse. Fire alarm designers and installers must be NICET Level III or IV certifiedf. Work in ceilings up to 60 feet high The project will involve the development and management of Contractor furnished submittals for items such as shop drawings, product data, commissioning plans, and contract close-out documentation as required by technical specifications of the task orders. Miscellaneous work within the project includes the delivery of Record Drawings.Placement of Task Orders. The actual amount of work to be performed and the time of such performance will be determined by a Contracting Officer who will issue written task orders. Prices will be requested and evaluated for each task order in accordance with FAR 16.505. The Government will evaluate price and past performance at a minimum but may include additional non-price factors. Each RFP will state the method of selection and any additional non-price factors. Whenever possible, award will be made without discussions. If discussions are required, each contractor included in the competitive range will be requested to provide a final proposal revision, unless eliminated from discussions.Important Note: The sam.gov response date listed elsewhere in this synopsis is for the sam.gov archive purposes only. It has no relationship to the actual proposal submission date. The proposal submission date will be contained in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments that are issued. When issued, the solicitation documents for this project will be available via sam.gov. No CDs OR HARD COPIES WILL BE AVAILABLE. Offerors are responsible for checking the reference page for any update(s) to the Notice. The Government is not responsible for any loss of Internet connectivity or for an offerors inability to access the document(s) posted at the referenced website. To obtain automatic notifications of updates to this solicitation, you MUST log in to sam.gov and add the solicitation to your watchlist. If you would like to list your firm so others can see you are an interested vendor, you must click the Add Me To Interested Vendors button in the listing for this solicitation on sam.gov.

title: Northwest Division Powerhouse Life Safety Upgrades Stage 1
description: Northwest Division Powerhouse Life Safety Upgrades Stage 1 The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Walla Walla District, intends to issue a single-phase solicitation on or about 30 November 2026 for a Construction Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple-Award Task Order Contract (MATOC). The anticipated MATOC will provide construction services for renovation and upgrade projects at hydroelectric powerhouses located at large, remote civil works projects within the Northwestern Division. The primary area of performance is anticipated to include USACE Walla Walla District projects at McNary, Ice Harbor, Lower Monumental, Little Goose, Lower Granite, and Dworshak. Task orders may also include work at other USACE projects within the Pacific Northwest, including locations within the Seattle and Portland Districts in Washington, Oregon, Idaho, and Montana. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Walla Walla District, anticipates awarding up to four (4) IDIQ MATOCs. At least one, and up to two, MATOCs will be reserved for award to qualified small business concerns. Task orders issued under the MATOCs will be firm-fixed-price. The aggregate shared contract capacity for all awarded MATOCs is anticipated to be $99 million. Each contract is anticipated to include a 36-month base period and two (2) 24-month option periods, exercisable at the Governments discretion. The Government may issue individual task orders with values up to $25,000,000. The Government reserves the right to issue additional solicitations and award additional contracts for the same or similar work within the geographic area covered by the MATOCs. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. This notice is for informational purposes only and is not a solicitation. The solicitation is anticipated to be issued on or about 30 November 2026. Summary Scope of Work: The purpose of this IDIQ MATOC is to provide construction services to renovate and upgrade life-safety systems at large hydroelectric powerhouses located at large, remote civil works projects. These powerhouses may range in size from 75,000 square feet to 420,000 square feet and from 5 stories to 11 stories. The work may consist of the following major industrial construction elements for installation and/or modification: 1. Fire detection and mass notification alarm systems 2. Wet pipe, fine water mist, and clean agent sprinkler fire suppression system(s) 3. Smoke control system, including stair pressurization fans, smoke exhaust fans, motorized fire-smoke dampers, and complex logic and programming matrix digital controls 4. HVAC direct digital controls 5. HVAC ventilation and conditioning equipment, dampers, and ductwork 6. Fabricated steel stairs and guardrails 7. Architectural fire barrier walls, fire doors, safety glazing and finishes 8. Firestopping 9. Emergency and exit lighting systems 10. Electrical power supply and distribution 11. Precast concrete 12. Low-slope roofing 13. Specific aspects of this project that may be especially challenging include: a. Robust industrial safety protocols with rigorous lockout tagout procedures b. Construction in a continuously operating industrial environment c. Proximity to high voltage equipment and transmission lines d. Multiple underground levels with limited access e. Fire alarm designers and installers must be NICET Level III or IV certified f. Work in ceilings up to 60 feet high The project will involve the development and management of Contractor furnished submittals for items such as shop drawings, product data, commissioning plans, and contract close-out documentation as required by technical specifications of the task orders. Miscellaneous work within the project includes the delivery of Record Drawings. Placement of Task Orders. The actual amount of work to be performed and the time of such performance will be determined by a Contracting Officer who will issue written task orders. Prices will be requested and evaluated for each task order in accordance with FAR 16.505. The Government will evaluate price and past performance at a minimum but may include additional non-price factors. Each RFP will state the method of selection and any additional non-price factors. Whenever possible, award will be made without discussions. If discussions are required, each contractor included in the competitive range will be requested to provide a final proposal revision, unless eliminated from discussions. description: The Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC), Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Fighters & Advanced Aircraft Directorate (AFLCMC/WA), F?15 System Program Office (AFLCMC/WAQ), Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB) is seeking sources for the procurement of an operationally qualified threat missile launch and approach warning system for rapid integration into the United States Air Force (USAF) F-15EX Eagle II fighter aircraft. title: RFP to Lease the Armstrong Dune Shack in Cape Cod National Seashore
description: SUMMARY OF LEASING OPPORTUNITY This Request for Proposals (RFP) provides the opportunity for any interested individual or organization, hereinafter referred to as �Offeror� to submit proposals to the National Park Service (NPS, �Lessor�) to lease NPS property at Cape Cod National Seashore for private, residential use and occupancy, under the following general terms and conditions. The selected offeror (Offeror,�you�,�your�) will have exclusive negotiation rights to enter a lease based on the attached Sample Lease (See Attachment A). Elements of your proposal may be incorporated into the Lease at Lessor�s discretion. Overview of Property Offered for Lease The �David and Connie Armstrong� (Armstrong) dune shack located with the Peaked Hill Bars Historic District of the Cape Cod National Seashore is available for lease to the public. The Peaked Hill Bars Historic District was determined to be eligible for the National Register of Historic Places in 1989 with formal listing in 2011. The Armstrong dune shack, located in Truro, MA, is one of eighteen (18) dune shacks located within the Historic District and listed on the National Register. It is the only Cape Cod National Seashore dune shack offered for lease at this time. The dune shack structures promote a simpler way of life. They lack many modern conveniences and amenities and have no municipal or commercial utilities. Access by motorized vehicle requires an NPS-issued off-road-vehicle (ORV) permit for the inner dune route, and a qualified 4-wheel drive truck, SUV, or car with appropriately aired down tires. Dune shacks are generally suitable to be used from Memorial Day to Labor Day. Access to the shacks during the off-season is predominantly for the purpose of maintenance, particularly to prepare for or clean-up after severe weather. Most dune shack occupants start the process of opening shacks for the summer beginning in April and securing them for the winter during the month of October. The Armstrong dune shack is the furthest east and most secluded shack in the district, standing approximately a half mile from its nearest neighbor. It is two stories; the upper level serves as the living area and the partial lower level is used for service and storage. The living space contains a wood-burning stove, water storage facilities and a gravity fed shower and toilet. A wrap-around deck serves as a seating and access area. Additional property details and site maps can be found in the Appendix. Allowed Uses of the Lease Premises Lessee may use the dune shack for private occupancy, in accordance with federal, state and local law. The dune shack must be maintained and operated as a traditional dune shack. Neither the property nor the lessee�s inner dune driving privileges may be used for commercial activities that provide goods, services, agreements or other functions for members, clients, or the public resulting in compensation, monetary gain, benefit or profit unless authorized via a separately obtained Commercial Use Authorization. Subleasing will not be allowed. Information regarding Commercial Use Authorizations (CUA) or Special Use Permits (SUP), can be found at these two sites: https://www.nps.gov/caco/getinvolved/commercial-use-authorizations.htm and https://www.nps.gov/caco/planyourvisit/special-use-permits.htm Key Information About This Leasing Opportunity Planned NPS Improvements: The property will be delivered to the Lessee �as-is with all faults�. Lessee Improvements: Subject to NPS approval, Lessee will be permitted to make Improvements subject to Building Code & Zoning and Historic Preservation guidelines provided below. Rent may be offset by the NPS-approved cost of completed Initial Improvements specified in the Appendix. Each offeror is responsible for verifying the condition of the property, developing a detailed scope of work and preparing a cost estimate for any proposed improvement plan. Generally, the lessee will not be able to upgrade amenities or expand the footprint of the shack. Expected Lease Commencement: The NPS anticipates the lease will commence in the late Spring of 2027. Building Codes & Zoning: For building codes and zoning, the Lease Premises are under exclusive jurisdiction of the Federal Government and are not subject to the zoning regulations of the Town of Truro or Barnstable County. However, the NPS will expect any work done on the property, where relevant, to meet the standards set forth by the 2024 ICC family of Codes and all codes referenced in those codes. For fire codes, follow all codes referenced in NPS Director�s Order #58 and NPS Reference Manual #58. Historic Preservation: Due to the historic nature of the offered property, the character-defining features of the building and surrounding landscape must be maintained. Any design and construction will be required to comply with one or more of the following: the Secretary of the Interior's Standards and Guidelines; National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) and Section 106 compliance; National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA); NFPA 914 Code for Protection of Historical Structures. Please note that your planned Improvements may trigger compliance processes in accordance with one or more of the laws, regulations or policies listed above. The cost of any such compliance process as well as the costs of plan check, code review and construction inspections will be borne by the Lessee. Jurisdiction For purposes except building codes and zoning the Lease Premises are subject to concurrent jurisdiction. Under concurrent jurisdiction, Federal and State governments share the governmental authority, and unless otherwise stated, the laws of both governments are applicable. The Lessee must comply, at its sole cost and expense, with all Applicable Laws and Requirements (including Federal, State, and local laws, rules, regulations, requirements, and policies) in fulfilling its obligations under the Lease. It is the responsibility of the Lessee to determine whether it is subject to specific taxes and assessments and abide by those applicable statutes. Any comments made by the NPS in this RFP do not alter those responsibilities, if any, nor should they be construed to take a position nor express a view on behalf of the Lessee. Term of the Lease Offerors may propose a Lease Term up to a maximum of ten (10) years. Rent NPS is required under 36 CFR Part 18 to receive, at a minimum, Fair Market Value Rent (FMVR). The amount of rent will be negotiated subsequently with the selected offeror, provided that the final rent must at least equal the FMVR as determined by the NPS. The Lessor may offset Rent for the approved costs of completed Initial Improvements incurred by the Lessee in accordance with the requirements of the Lease. The Fair Market Value Annual Rent for the first year of the lease is $10,250.00. This rent will be subject to an annual Consumer Price Index (CPI) adjustment. Insurance During the term of this Lease, the Lessee shall maintain adequate Property and General Liability insurance coverage. Further information regarding insurance requirements can be found in Attachment A: Sample Lease. Insurance coverage amounts will be periodically reviewed by the NPS. These reviews seek to confirm that a Lessee has appropriate coverage considering any changing circumstances. Utilities The Armstrong shack does not have access to commercial utilities such as electricity, municipal water or municipal sewage systems. Alternative primitive systems, such as hand pumps and a wood stove have been used by current and prior occupants and most such systems are permitted for continued use. The gravity fed indoor toilet that empties into an approximate 100-gallon metal receptacle buried in the sand will not be permitted for continued use and must be replaced by an incinerating toilet or other acceptable alternative that meets current federal, state or local environmental regulations. Conventional utilities will not be extended to the dune shack.

title: A Study on Vessel Design Challenge
description: The purpose of amendment no. 2 is to respond to the following questions. Question-4. Is MARAD open to all forms of propulsion to gain fuel efficiencies - for example, hybrid diesel-electric equipment with electric motors and batteries? Response-4. There are no limits or specific requirements for the type of propulsion or fuel. Technologies, including fuels and propulsion, should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). description: U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) A Study on Vessel Design Challenge RFP No. 693JF726R000016 REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP): The Maritime Administration�s (MARAD) Maritime Environmental and Technical Assistance (META) program is issuing a request for proposals (RFP) for a Vessel Design Challenge (Challenge). This Challenge intends to fund multiple design teams willing to undertake integrated design work to improve fuel efficiency and reduce vessel underwater radiated noise (URN) to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Individual awards depend on number of designs proposed for the package. Awards are intended to be for not less than $150k and likely not more than $450k. Project completion timeline is 12-18 months. Total funding available is up to $1.25 million. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The META program (46 U.S.C. � 50307) is investigating the interconnections between broader fuel efficiency, reducing URN from vessels, and exploring potential co-benefits. It is the policy of the United States to revitalize and rebuild domestic maritime industries and workforce to promote national security and economic prosperity. Accomplishing this requires making United States-flagged and built vessels commercially competitive in international commerce, rebuilding America�s maritime manufacturing capabilities, and expanding and strengthening the recruitment, training, and retention of the relevant workforce. The most promising opportunities for optimizing fuel efficiency gains and achieving URN reductions are in the early ship design stage, using a systems approach. This requires intentional and integrated ship designs that prioritize fuel efficiency while simultaneously reducing URN. Advanced fluid dynamic modeling enables comparison among hull, engine, and propeller design and arrangement, providing valuable information to the industry about the return on investment (ROI) for various technology and design optimizations at the design phase. Individual technologies claim to provide efficiency and noise reduction benefits, but the additive cost-savings have not been quantified for applying technologies in series and demonstrating increased efficiencies across multiple areas. Recently published studies summarized the state of knowledge and availability of technologies that can be applied to vessels to improve energy efficiency while reducing vessel generated URN. Those reports crosswalk not only the interoperability of technologies and design elements, but the potential reductions, costs, and return on investment. The next phase is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. By using this approach, Teams will begin at the drawing table to quantify the benefits of innovative technology integration into the design phase for application on new vessels. The Vessel Design Challenge is intended to facilitate the demonstration of novel vessel designs that meet or exceed international benchmarks for fuel efficiency and URN source levels. This Challenge is intended to fund multiple Design Teams willing to undertake this kind of integrated design work to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. PROPOSAL CONTENT Proposed Vessel Design: Design proposals can include: Existing projects that would be redesigned, Forthcoming projects that are just beginning the design specification phase, and Designs that are theoretical or more experimental which aim to create a new approach or design. There are no restrictions on eligible vessels, however, given the mission of the Maritime Administration, vessels should be commercially useful and generally would not include small watercraft, recreational vessels, or fisheries vessels. Eligible designs include vessels operating in coastal or inland waterways as well as the Great Lakes. Ideal proposals will be for new design approaches or design modifications that couple hull-machinery-propulsion approaches to maximize fuel efficiency, URN reduction, and ROI. Technologies should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Design Team: The approach to the Challenge will include a design team. Teams should include description of partnerships, collaborations, and/or processes that will ensure success of the proposal. Further, proposals should identify the Team�s capabilities, related experience, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve project goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Development of an ideal team should represent the concept of a design-build approach and include: Naval architect(s) Marine Engineer(s) Shipyard(s) Owner/operator/buyer (can be more than one) Technology provider(s) (including fuel supplier, as needed) May include operator/charter party, BCO, logistics partners, port/city/public entity, private financing partner. Teams may submit one or more vessel designs to the Challenge. Funding amounts will be based on: the number of vessel designs proposed their technology innovation, or a combination thereof One or all proposed designs may be funded depending on proposals. There is no limit to number of teams an organization can participate in, however, an organization may only �lead� one team/proposal. No identical teams with rotating �leads� will be permitted. Preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag Methods: Proposals must include a detailed description of the design and modeling approaches that will be used to meet the Design Challenge Parameters as noted below, including those for fuel burn estimates and URN source level as well as modeling for return on investment and similar economic estimates and valuations. Timeline: The proposed plan should include the expected timeline (not to exceed 18 months) inclusive of kick off meetings with MARAD, design and technology integration and assessment, interim progress report detailing vessel design and technology application progress, data collection and analysis, and final report deliverables. Budget: All proposals must include a compete, detailed, and justifiable budget with general line items for various design components and stages including fuel, URN, and ROI evaluation and calculations. Budgets should demonstrate market conditions or similar that support these budget estimates. Description of key personnel, qualifications, and expected level of effort should also be included. Proposals may also include any additional considerations, outreach, or analysis recommended to achieve the goals of the project. Design Challenge Parameters Design specifications: The objective is for designs to meet or exceed these specifications for fuel efficiency improvement and noise reduction. Recognizing that this is a demonstration of technical feasibility and economic achievability, if these design specifications are not achievable, alternative efficiency and noise improvements should be documented demonstrating the current limits of technologies. These specifications should be considered aspirational to test the limits of the possible within the bounds of the practical. Energy Efficiency: 30% efficiency improvement over a typical vessel design with conventional hull and machinery arrangements and fuels. Individual awards depend on number of designs proposed for the package. Awards are intended to be for not less than $150k and likely not more than $450k. Project completion timeline is 12-18 months. Total funding available is up to $1.25 million. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The META program (46 U.S.C. � 50307) is investigating the interconnections between broader fuel efficiency, reducing URN from vessels, and exploring potential co-benefits. It is the policy of the United States to revitalize and rebuild domestic maritime industries and workforce to promote national security and economic prosperity. Accomplishing this requires making United States-flagged and built vessels commercially competitive in international commerce, rebuilding America�s maritime manufacturing capabilities, and expanding and strengthening the recruitment, training, and retention of the relevant workforce. The most promising opportunities for optimizing fuel efficiency gains and achieving URN reductions are in the early ship design stage, using a systems approach. This requires intentional and integrated ship designs that prioritize fuel efficiency while simultaneously reducing URN. Advanced fluid dynamic modeling enables comparison among hull, engine, and propeller design and arrangement, providing valuable information to the industry about the return on investment (ROI) for various technology and design optimizations at the design phase. Individual technologies claim to provide efficiency and noise reduction benefits, but the additive cost-savings have not been quantified for applying technologies in series and demonstrating increased efficiencies across multiple areas. Recently published studies summarized the state of knowledge and availability of technologies that can be applied to vessels to improve energy efficiency while reducing vessel generated URN. Those reports crosswalk not only the interoperability of technologies and design elements, but the potential reductions, costs, and return on investment. The next phase is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. By using this approach, Teams will begin at the drawing table to quantify the benefits of innovative technology integration into the design phase for application on new vessels. The Vessel Design Challenge is intended to facilitate the demonstration of novel vessel designs that meet or exceed international benchmarks for fuel efficiency and URN source levels. This Challenge is intended to fund multiple Design Teams willing to undertake this kind of integrated design work to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. PROPOSAL CONTENT Proposed Vessel Design: Design proposals can include: Existing projects that would be redesigned, Forthcoming projects that are just beginning the design specification phase, and Designs that are theoretical or more experimental which aim to create a new approach or design. There are no restrictions on eligible vessels, however, given the mission of the Maritime Administration, vessels should be commercially useful and generally would not include small watercraft, recreational vessels, or fisheries vessels. Eligible designs include vessels operating in coastal or inland waterways as well as the Great Lakes. Ideal proposals will be for new design approaches or design modifications that couple hull-machinery-propulsion approaches to maximize fuel efficiency, URN reduction, and ROI. Technologies should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Design Team: The approach to the Challenge will include a design team. Teams should include description of partnerships, collaborations, and/or processes that will ensure success of the proposal. Further, proposals should identify the Team�s capabilities, related experience, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve project goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Development of an ideal team should represent the concept of a design-build approach and include: Naval architect(s) Marine Engineer(s) Shipyard(s) Owner/operator/buyer (can be more than one) Technology provider(s) (including fuel supplier, as needed) May include operator/charter party, BCO, logistics partners, port/city/public entity, private financing partner. Teams may submit one or more vessel designs to the Challenge. Funding amounts will be based on: the number of vessel designs proposed their technology innovation, or a combination thereof One or all proposed designs may be funded depending on proposals. There is no limit to number of teams an organization can participate in, however, an organization may only �lead� one team/proposal. No identical teams with rotating �leads� will be permitted. Preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag Methods: Proposals must include a detailed description of the design and modeling approaches that will be used to meet the Design Challenge Parameters as noted below, including those for fuel burn estimates and URN source level as well as modeling for return on investment and similar economic estimates and valuations. Timeline: The proposed plan should include the expected timeline (not to exceed 18 months) inclusive of kick off meetings with MARAD, design and technology integration and assessment, interim progress report detailing vessel design and technology application progress, data collection and analysis, and final report deliverables. Budget: All proposals must include a compete, detailed, and justifiable budget with general line items for various design components and stages including fuel, URN, and ROI evaluation and calculations. Budgets should demonstrate market conditions or similar that support these budget estimates. Description of key personnel, qualifications, and expected level of effort should also be included. Proposals may also include any additional considerations, outreach, or analysis recommended to achieve the goals of the project. Design Challenge Parameters Design specifications: The objective is for designs to meet or exceed these specifications for fuel efficiency improvement and noise reduction. Recognizing that this is a demonstration of technical feasibility and economic achievability, if these design specifications are not achievable, alternative efficiency and noise improvements should be documented demonstrating the current limits of technologies. These specifications should be considered aspirational to test the limits of the possible within the bounds of the practical. Energy Efficiency: 30% efficiency improvement over a typical vessel design with conventional hull and machinery arrangements and fuels. buyer: Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie GmbH (HZB)
title: Germany – Laboratory, optical and precision equipments (excl. glasses) – V358_2026 - CE-NDEI - Extension of XPS Erlangen (HI-ERN)
description: Das Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie GmbH (HZB) ist ein unabhängiges wissenschaftliches Forschungszentrum unter dem Dach der Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft mit Standorten in Berlin-Adlershof und Wannsee. Der Elektronen-Speicherring BESSY II liefert hochbrillante Synchrotronstrahlung – vom Terahertz- bis in den Röntgenbereich. Mit seinem Schwerpunkt auf VUV- und weicher Röntgenstrahlung eignet sich BESSY II hervorragend für die Analyse von Energiematerialien und Dünnschichtsystemen. Die Weiterentwicklung der Instrumentierung sowie die Erarbeitung eines Konzepts für eine Nachfolgequelle (BESSY III) zählen zu den wichtigsten Aufgaben der kommenden Jahre. An unserem Elektronen-Speicherring BESSY II verzeichnen wir jährlich durchschnittlich 2700 Besuche von Gastforschenden aus 28 Ländern. Jährlich erscheinen 500 bis 600 wissenschaftliche Publikationen, die auf Messungen an BESSY II (sowie bis Ende 2019 auch an BER II) basieren. Gruppe CE-NDEI Die Forschungsaktivitäten der Gruppe „Dynamic Electrocatalytic Interfaces“ (CE-NDEI) konzentrieren sich darauf, die dynamischen Veränderungen katalytischer Oberflächen unter realen Reaktionsbedingungen zu verstehen. Die Gruppe konzipiert und fertigt nanostrukturierte, katalytisch aktive Dünnschicht-Modelloberflächen. Sie untersucht systematisch die strukturellen und zusammensetzungsbezogenen Veränderungen, die während katalytischer Prozesse auftreten, sowie deren Einfluss auf Reaktionsmechanismen und Kinetik in der Elektrokatalyse. Diese Forschung erfolgt durch eine Kombination komplementärer *ex-situ*- und *in-situ*-Experimentierverfahren. Ein zentrales Ziel ist ein detailliertes mechanistisches Verständnis chemischer Prozesse an komplexen, sich dynamisch entwickelnden Grenzflächen – insbesondere bei elektrokatalytischen Reaktionen, die für Technologien zur Energieumwandlung und Energiespeicherung relevant sind. Letztlich zielt die Arbeit darauf ab, die Stabilitätsgrenzen von Elektrokatalysatormaterialien zu überwinden. Das methodische Spektrum der Gruppe umfasst eine Vielzahl physikalischer Gasphasenabscheidungsverfahren (PVD), moderne elektrochemische Charakterisierungsmethoden, Atomsonden-Tomographie sowie Röntgen-Photoelektronenspektroskopie – einschließlich Messungen an Synchrotronstrahlungsquellen. Die Arbeitsgruppe ist am Helmholtz-Institut Erlangen-Nürnberg für Erneuerbare Energien (HI ERN) angesiedelt und arbeitet eng mit dem HI ERN, dem Forschungszentrum Jülich (FZJ) sowie der Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU) zusammen. Erweiterung der XPS-Kapazitäten der Arbeitsgruppe CE-NDEI Um die Forschungsmöglichkeiten der Arbeitsgruppe CE-NDEI am HZB auszubauen und die Zusammenarbeit mit dem HI ERN sowie der FAU im Bereich der In-situ-Charakterisierung von Mehrkomponenten-Katalysatormaterialien zu fördern, ist die Anschaffung eines laborbasierten Systems zur Röntgenabsorptionsfeinstruktur-Analyse (XAFS) geplant. Dieses System ermöglicht die In-situ-Untersuchung der elektronischen Struktur von Katalysatoren auf Basis von Übergangsmetallen – sowohl im Transmissions- als auch im Fluoreszenzmodus – und deckt einen Energiebereich von etwa 4,5 bis 25 keV ab (weitere Spezifikationen finden Sie in der separaten technischen Beschreibung). Durch die Ergänzung der bereits vorhandenen Möglichkeiten zur Röntgenphotoelektronenspektroskopie (XPS) in der Arbeitsgruppe CE-NDEI erlaubt der neue XAFS-Aufbau detaillierte Einblicke in die lokale elektronische und strukturelle Umgebung aktiver Katalysatorkomponenten unter realistischen Betriebsbedingungen. Dieser Fortschritt wird das Verständnis von Struktur-Funktions-Beziehungen in katalytischen Systemen maßgeblich vertiefen. Zudem dürfte die Implementierung dieses laborbasierten XAFS-Systems das Interesse von Forschenden am HI ERN/FZJ sowie an der FAU an In-situ-Spektroskopieverfahren – einschließlich der am BESSY II verfügbaren synchrotronbasierten Methoden – steigern. Auf diese Weise wird die strategische Zusammenarbeit zwischen dem HZB, dem HI ERN und dem FZJ weiter gestärkt. Gemäß Beschreibung der technischen und funktionalen Mindestanforderungen soll ein laborbasiertes Röntgenspektrometer für die Röntgenabsorptionsfeinstruktur-Analyse (XAFS) beschafft werden, das optional auch Röntgenemissionsspektroskopie (XES) ermöglicht. Das Gerät soll in der Lage sein, XANES- und EXAFS-Daten von einer Qualität zu liefern, die mit der an Synchrotronanlagen erzielbaren Qualität vergleichbar ist. Dies soll Forschung und Entwicklung in Bereichen wie Materialwissenschaften, Katalyse, Energiematerialien und verwandten Feldern ermöglichen, ohne dass ein Zugang zu Synchrotronanlagen erforderlich ist. Die technischen Spezifikationen sowie der Leistungsumfang für den Auftragnehmer hinsichtlich der mechanischen Konstruktion und des Baus des Spektrometers sind in den Vergabeunterlagen festgeschrieben. Die Einhaltung dieser Spezifikationen ist durch geeignete Methoden nachzuweisen. Das System muss für den regulären Laboreinsatz geeignet sein und den geltenden Sicherheitsnormen entsprechen. Der Aufbau muss gewährleisten, dass Proben unter den definierten Spezifikationen untersucht werden können.

title: Norway – Construction work – U2940 EFU-10988 Storetveit school - procurement of a turnkey contractor
description: Bergen municipality, the Development Department, hereby invites tenderers to a competition for a contract for a turnkey contract in the project U2940 Storetveit School. Storetveit secondary school needs upgrading and expanded capacity to meet the current educational and technical requirements, in addition to the expected increase in pupil numbers. The school ́s student capacity shall be increased from 450 to 600 pupils. The existing school building shall be renovated and reconstructed. In addition, two buildings shall be demolished and a new building shall be constructed, including a sports hall. The project also involves upgrading of outside areas for both the school and Storetveit nursery, as well as order requirements connected to, among other things, traffic safety, upgrading of roads, spaces and tracks.

title: Norway – Research services – Openness and inclusion - police interaction with the entire population
description: The aim of the research assignment is to obtain knowledge about how different groups of the population experience the police, what conditions affect the interaction between police and inhabitants, and how the police can ensure that different perspectives and experiences are heard and safeguarded. There is a need for knowledge about whether there are groups that find that they are not heard, how the police reach out to groups that to a small degree contact the police on their own initiative and how different forms of communication and dialogue are experienced by different groups. The research shall provide a better knowledge basis for how the police can strengthen the dialogue with the population, adapt communication and work forms to different target groups and develop services that safeguard legal security, equal treatment and high quality. The research shall also contribute with knowledge on the connection between transparency, inclusion, trust and the police's legitimacy, as well as the impact this can have on society's resilience. See further information in the tender documentation.

title: Norway – Research services – Openness and inclusion - police interaction with the entire population
description: The aim of the research assignment is to obtain knowledge about how different groups of the population experience the police, what conditions affect the interaction between police and inhabitants, and how the police can ensure that different perspectives and experiences are heard and safeguarded. There is a need for knowledge about whether there are groups that find that they are not heard, how the police reach out to groups that to a small degree contact the police on their own initiative and how different forms of communication and dialogue are experienced by different groups. The research shall provide a better knowledge basis for how the police can strengthen the dialogue with the population, adapt communication and work forms to different target groups and develop services that safeguard legal security, equal treatment and high quality. The research shall also contribute with knowledge on the connection between transparency, inclusion, trust and the police's legitimacy, as well as the impact this can have on society's resilience. description: Le marché porte sur l’étude et la construction en Entreprise Totale des parties d’ouvrages suivantes : 1. Nouvelle station de découplage (SDD) y compris les adaptations hydrauliques dans les stations de pompage (SPP), les conduites de liaison SPP et SDD et les conduites de rejet au lac entre le bâtiment SDD et la chambre de visite d’interface des conduites CCU/SDD. 2. Nouvelles conduites de liaison (terrestres) SDD-PDR jusqu’au poste de redistribution PDR, y compris la création d’un nouveau local de pompes dans l’actuel parking au sous-sol du bâtiment BS de l’EPFL. 3. Rénovation du réseau de distribution dans les galeries EPFL depuis le poste PDR jusqu’aux différentes sous-stations propres à chaque bâtiment du campus y compris la nouvelle conduite de retour et les adaptations hydrauliques à la CCT. L’Entreprise Totale interviendra de la phase « 32. Projet d’ouvrage » jusqu’à la phase « 53. Mise en service, achèvement ». L’élément déclencheur et l’objectif primordial du projet est la protection contre la prolifération des moules Quagga dans nos conduites et la sécurisation du réseau de refroidissement. Cependant, la vétusté des conduites ainsi que nos capacités en refroidissement actuelles, induisent une réflexion globale sur l’avenir de l’ensemble du site de l’EPFL et l’UNIL à Ecublens. De ce fait, le projet comprend les trois objectifs ci-dessous : 1. Protection totale des conduites du réseau de refroidissement contre la prolifération des moules Quagga, grâce au découplage hydraulique et à un nouveau réseau en boucle fermée. 2. Augmentation des capacités en refroidissement afin de subvenir aux besoins futurs dus aux nouveaux bâtiments et à l’augmentation de la demande des bâtiments existants. 3. Réduction des coûts d’exploitation et optimisation énergétique grâce au bouclage du réseau. Veuillez consulter le cahier des charges et ses annexes pour plus de renseignement.

description: Die Hanse- und Universitätsstadt Rostock plant den Neubau eines Hortgebäudes. Die künftige Bebauung besteht aus einem Baukörper mit einem 2-geschossigen Hortgebäude und einem 1-geschossigen Mensa-Anbau, die ohne Unterkellerung geplant werden. Das Hortgebäude nimmt in 7 Horträumen und 2 teilbaren Förderräumen insgesamt Platz für 176 Hortkinder und Horterzieher auf. Sanitärräume sind in beiden Geschossen verteilt. Die Mittelzonen werden im Erdgeschoß für Empfang und Garderobenschränke genutzt. Im Obergeschoß befindet sich hier eine zusätzliche Fläche für Aktivitäten. Alle Ebenen sind barrierefrei erreichbar. Das Hortgebäude verfügt zudem über einen separaten Hofausgang mit daneben liegender Außen-Toilette. Hort und Mensa werden über einen gemeinsamen Eingangsbereich erschlossen. In diesem Mittelbau sind WC-Räume inkl. einem barrierefreien WC erreichbar. Das barrierefreie WC ist zudem mit einer Duschecke ausgestattet. Die Mensa steht insbesondere den Grundschülern der Schmarler Grundschule zur Verfügung und wird über die zentrale Mittagsversorgung der Hansestadt Rostock betrieben. Die Ausgabeküche versorgt dann ca. 320 Nutzer. Eine Nutzung des Mensaraumes im Rahmen des Schulbetriebes und für Veranstaltungen des Hortes soll möglich sein. Auf den Dächern der Gebäudeteile befinden sich die zugeordneten Lüftungs- und Kälteanlagen. Die Dachfläche des Hortes wird über das Fluchttreppenhaus erschlossen. Das Dach erhält eine extensive Dachbegrünung als Retentionsdach. Das Mensadach erhält zudem eine PV-Anlage, ebenfalls mit Dachbegrünung. Die Außenanlagengestaltung beinhaltet die Grünflächen und Wege unter Berücksichtigung des Sporthallenzuganges und Flächen für die Feuerwehr. Parkplätze für PKW, teilweise mit ELT-Ladesäulen (nur Vorrüstung) werden vor dem Haupteingang angeordnet. Abstellplätze für Fahrräder werden auf dem Grundstück verteilt.

title: Netherlands – Software package and information systems – Sociaal Domein-software
description: Gemeente Nijkerk is voornemens een Opdracht te verstrekken voor de (her-)verwerving van haar Sociaal Domein-software. Gemeente Nijkerk wenst, vanwege het verlopen van de huidige contracten met Centric Digitale Overheid voor het gebruik van Suite4SociaalDomein en WIZportaal van Stipter en aanverwanten, een zo integraal mogelijke ICT-oplossing voor het Sociaal Domein via een openbare Europese aanbesteding in de markt te zetten. De beoogde ICT-oplossing wordt geleverd in SaaS-vorm. Eveneens wordt het technisch beheer ten aanzien van deze Oplossing door de leverancier in de service inbegrepen en meegeleverd. Het functioneel beheer van de Oplossing geschiedt zo veel mogelijk door Gemeente Nijkerk zelf. De Oplossing bestaat bij voorkeur uit één systeem dat tevens mag bestaan uit een samenhangende combinatie van producten en diensten, maar één Opdrachtnemer en één aanspreekpunt voor de gehele combinatie gedurende de looptijd van de Overeenkomst dient te hebben. Geraamde waarde betreft €3.335.000 over de gehele contractduur van 13 jaar. Zie voor meer toelichting de aanbestedingsleidraad.

De maximale waarde van de raamovereenkomst voor gemeente Veendam is € 2.140.000,- exclusief BTW (over de totale duur van vier jaar inclusief verlengingsopties). De gemeente is gerechtigd de raamovereenkomst te beëindigen als voor het einde van de overeengekomen contractduur de maximale waarde aan opdrachten onder de raamovereenkomst is bereikt. title: Belgium – Hotel, restaurant and retail trade services – CONCESSION DE SERVICES RELATIVE À L'AMÉNAGEMENT, À L'ANIMATION ET À L'EXPLOITATION DU SITE DE FALEMPRISE
description: Le site de Falemprise offre près de cinq hectares de terrain en bord de lac, une plage, une plaine, des équipements de loisirs et un bâtiment d'accueil. Le Concédant ne recherche pas un simple exploitant d'équipements : il recherche un partenaire capable de révéler le potentiel du Site, pour en faire une destination à part entière, où l'on vient pour elle-même, où l'on reste et où l'on revient, et qui donne envie de découvrir le reste du Domaine. Objet. La Concession a pour objet de confier à un concessionnaire unique, pour la durée fixée conformément à l'article III.2 : - la conception d'un Programme de destination touristique pour l'ensemble du Site ; - la réalisation, à ses frais et risques, du Programme d'investissements nécessaire à ce projet, à l'exclusion des Travaux d'amorçage ; - l'exploitation, l'animation, la commercialisation et l'entretien du Site ; - la mise en œuvre et le maintien du Socle d'intérêt général. L'exploitation s'inscrit dans la mission confiée au Concédant par le Contrat de gestion, consistant à développer et exploiter un « site exemplaire en matière de tourisme durable ». Le Concessionnaire contribue aux objectifs et aux indicateurs qui en découlent, dans les conditions prévues par la Convention.

title: Subvergabe Linienbündel Bad Mergentheim
description: Die Stadtverkehr Bad Mergentheim GmbH beabsichtigt als Inhaber der Genehmigung für den Betrieb des Linienbündels Bad Mergentheim nach einem neuen Konzept nach der Sektorenverordnung (SektVO) gemäß § 13 SektVO i. V. m. § 100 Abs. 1 Nr.1 und 102 Abs. 4 GWB mit Betriebsaufnahme zum 01.01.2028 zu vergeben. Der Verkehrsverbund Rhein-Neckar GmbH — B1 3-5, 68159 Mannheim — führt als Vergabestelle die Vergabe im Namen der Stadtverkehr Bad Mergentheim durch. Folgende Regelungen zur Tariftreue und Sozialstandards sind zur Sicherung der Betriebsqualität Teil der ausreichenden Verkehrsbedienung: Aufgrund der Arbeitsmarktsituation in der Metropolregion Rhein-Neckar und der Wirtschaftsregionen Vorderpfalz und Rheinhessen wird der künftige Betreiber verpflichtet, seinen Beschäftigten zur Sicherung einer aus-reichenden Qualifikation des Fahrpersonals bei der Ausführung der Leistung mindestens gemäß LTMG entsprechend der repräsentativ erklärten Tarifverträgen festgelegte Entgelt zu zahlen sowie die in diesen Tarifverträgen festgelegten Arbeitsbedingungen zu garantieren. Weitere Vorgaben finden Sie unter: https://www.landesrecht-bw.de/jportal/portal/page/bsbawueprod.psml/action/portlets.jw.MainAction? eventSubmit_doNavigate=searchInSubtreeTOC&showdoccase=1&doc.id=jlr- Tarift_MindLohnGBWpP8. Diese Verpflichtung gilt für die gesamte Laufzeit des neuen Vertragszeitraumes dynamisch, also stets mit Bezug auf die jeweils noch erfolgenden Anpassungen der Tarifverträge in der Zukunft. Erfolgt der Einsatz von Subunternehmern, haben diese ebenfalls die Einhaltung dieser Verpflichtungen zu garantieren. Zusätzlich zu den tarifvertraglich zu garantierenden Sozialstandards gelten für alle eingesetzten Fahrerinnen und Fahrer folgende Bedingungen zu Lenkzeitunterbrechungen und Pausen: Tarifvertraglich nicht als Arbeitszeit geltende Lenkzeitunterbrechungen und Pausen dürfen je Schichtmaximal 60 Minuten betragen. Überschreiten die Lenkzeitunterbrechungen und Pausen diese Grenze, sind die 60-Minuten-Grenze überschreitenden Zeiten der Arbeitsunterbrechungen der Arbeitszeit zuzurechnen. Als echte, nicht zu vergütende Freizeit im Sinne eines geteilten Dienstes zählt eine einmalige Arbeitsunterbrechung je Schicht von mind. 2 Std, die am Wohnort (Stadtteil) des Mitarbeiters oder an einem Betriebsstandort mit adäquaten Sozialräumen beginnen und enden. Die Vorhaltung von Sozialräumen ist in diesem Zusammenhang nicht relevant, sofern die Arbeitsunterbrechung länger als 4 Std dauert. Folgende Regelungen zur Personalübernahme sind ebenfalls zur Sicherung der Betriebsqualität Teil der ausreichenden Verkehrsbedienung: Die Bieter verpflichten sich im Rahmen ihres Angebotes, denjenigen Fahrer/innen einen Arbeitsvertrag anzubieten, die während der Vergabe im Betrieb des Altbetreibers des Linienbündels mindestens mit 70 % der regulären Arbeitszeit eingesetzt sind und die zum Zeitpunkt der Inbetriebnahme einen gültigen Arbeitsvertrag mit dem Altbetreiber vorweisen können. Der neue Arbeitsvertrag ist unbefristet und ohne Probezeit abzuschließen. Grundlage des Einstellungsangebotes müssen die im Unternehmen des Konzessionsnehmers für die übrige Belegschaft geltenden tarifvertraglichen und in Betriebsvereinbarungen geregelten Konditionen sein. Sofern der im übernehmenden Unternehmen praktizierte Tarifvertrag die Höhe des Entgeltes sowie die Zahl der Urlaubstage von der Dauer der Betriebszugehörigkeit abhängig gestaltet, muss der neue Anstellungsvertrag vorsehen, dass die Betriebszugehörigkeit beim Altbetreiber im Rahmen der entgeltlichen Eingruppierung und Urlaubsgewährung wie eine Betriebszugehörigkeit im übernehmenden Unternehmen gewertet wird.

buyer: Eigenbetrieb Kommunale Objektbewirtschaftung und -entwicklung der Hanse- und Universitätsstadt Rostock
title: Neubau Hortgebäude, St.-Jantzen-Ring 3-6, 18106 Rostock - Los 501 - Leitungsbau
description: Die Hanse- und Universitätsstadt Rostock plant den Neubau eines Hortgebäudes. Die künftige Bebauung besteht aus einem Baukörper mit einem 2-geschossigen Hortgebäude und einem 1-geschossigen Mensa-Anbau, die ohne Unterkellerung geplant werden. Das Hortgebäude nimmt in 7 Horträumen und 2 teilbaren Förderräumen insgesamt Platz für 176 Hortkinder und Horterzieher auf. Sanitärräume sind in beiden Geschossen verteilt. Die Mittelzonen werden im Erdgeschoß für Empfang und Garderobenschränke genutzt. Im Obergeschoß befindet sich hier eine zusätzliche Fläche für Aktivitäten. Alle Ebenen sind barrierefrei erreichbar. Das Hortgebäude verfügt zudem über einen separaten Hofausgang mit daneben liegender Außen-Toilette. Hort und Mensa werden über einen gemeinsamen Eingangsbereich erschlossen. In diesem Mittelbau sind WC-Räume inkl. einem barrierefreien WC erreichbar. Das barrierefreie WC ist zudem mit einer Duschecke ausgestattet. Die Mensa steht insbesondere den Grundschülern der Schmarler Grundschule zur Verfügung und wird über die zentrale Mittagsversorgung der Hansestadt Rostock betrieben. Die Ausgabeküche versorgt dann ca. 320 Nutzer. Eine Nutzung des Mensaraumes im Rahmen des Schulbetriebes und für Veranstaltungen des Hortes soll möglich sein. Auf den Dächern der Gebäudeteile befinden sich die zugeordneten Lüftungs- und Kälteanlagen. Die Dachfläche des Hortes wird über das Fluchttreppenhaus erschlossen. Das Dach erhält eine extensive Dachbegrünung als Retentionsdach. Das Mensadach erhält zudem eine PV-Anlage, ebenfalls mit Dachbegrünung. Die Außenanlagengestaltung beinhaltet die Grünflächen und Wege unter Berücksichtigung des Sporthallenzuganges und Flächen für die Feuerwehr. title: Sallilan koulun, A-osa, purkaminen
description: Sallilan koulun, A-osa, purkaminen Huittisten kaupunki pyytää tarjouksia (KVR-urakka) Sallilan koulurakennuksen A-osan ja siihen liittyvän B-osaan vievän yhdyskanaalin sekä maan alla olevan öljysäiliön purkamisesta. Hanke sisältää purkutyön suunnittelun, purkutyöt, purkujätteiden jätehuollon ja purkualueen siistimisen sekä kuoppien ja kaivantojen tasaamisen. Purkukohde on 1970-luvun lopulla rakennettu Sallilan koulun A-osa, joka sijaitsee osoitteessa Sallilantie 63, Vampula, Huittinen. Rakennukseen kuuluu liitteen 3 mukaiset tilat. Purettavan A-osan kerrosala on n. 1360 m2. Rakennus poistetaan käytöstä 6.6.2027, jonka jälkeen Huittisten kaupunki tyhjentää sen tarvittavilta osin kalusteista 7.-11.6.2027 välisenä aikana sekä katkaisee/siirtää B-osaan liittymät. Purkutyön ja luovutuksen tilaajalle on tapahduttava 14.6.2027- 16.7.2027 välisenä aikana. Uuden koulurakennuksen ja päiväkodin rakentaminen alkaa 19.7.2027 purettavan rakennuksen paikalle. Purettava koulurakennus ja yhdyskanaali liittyvät kiinteästi samassa rakennuskokonaisuudessa edelleen toimivaan B-rakennukseen, mikä tulee ottaa huomioon purkutöiden suunnittelussa. Tärkeää on huomioida turvallisuus ja purkutyössä syntyvän pölyn hallinta. Purkutyöstä ei saa aiheutua vaaraa tai haittaa naapurustolle. Purkualue on aidattava niin, että ulkopuoliset eivät missään olosuhteissa pääse työmaa-alueelle. Lisäksi purkutyömaan välittömässä läheisyydessä sijaitsee liikunta-alue. Purku-urakan suorituksessa noudatetaan pääsääntöisesti Ympäristöministeriön julkaisua. Purkutyöt-opas tekijöille ja teettäjille, lisäksi urakassa tulee noudattaa ja ottaa huomioon: -rakentamislaki ja muu rakentamista sekä purkamista koskeva lainsäädäntö -työturvallisuuslainsäädäntö -asbestilainsäädäntö -jätelainsäädäntö -ympäristölainsäädäntö -muu lainsäädäntö mm. terveydensuojelulaki -Huittisten kaupungin rakennusjärjestys, ympäristönsuojelumääräykset ja jätehuoltomääräykset -pääurakoitsija pitää työmaapäiväkirjaa ja työmaan tarkastusasiakirjaa, osallistuu tarvittaessa työmaakokouksiin ja kutsuu kunnan rakennusvalvontaviranomaisen purkutyön loppukatselmukseen ennen purkutyön luovutusta tilaajalle. Kaikki yllä mainittujen ja muiden purkutöitä koskevien lakien, asetusten ja määräysten edellyttämät luvat, suunnitelmat, ilmoitukset, todistukset, tarkastukset, siirtoasiakirjat yms. hankkii ja tarvittaessa ao. viranomaiselle toimittaa purku-urakkaan kuuluvana purku-urakoitsija. Purkukohteen perustukset on poistettava kokonaisuudessaan. Alue on siistittävä ja tasattava puhdasta hiekkaa käyttäen. Purkuluvan hoitaa ja maksaa Huittisten kaupunki. Valittava purku-urakoitsija arvioi määrät ja loppusijoituspaikat purkulupahakemusta varten. Purettavat rakennusosat, sekä purkujäte (myös asbesti, haitalliset jätteet, ongelmajätteet jne., lajitteluineen, poiskuljetuksineen, jäteveroineen, kierrätyksineen ja kaatopaikkamaksuineen kuuluvat purku-urakoitsijalle. Ne on toimitettava tarvittavat luvat omaaviin rakennusjätteen vastaanottopaikkoihin. Kohteeseen on tehty haitta-ainekartoitus (liitteet 5 ja 6). Asbestia ja muita haitta-aineita sisältävät materiaalit kuuluvat purku-urakkaan, minkä vuoksi tarjoajien on hyvä tutustua kohteeseen etukäteen joko 30.11.2026 klo 14.00-15.00 suoritettavassa näytössä tai 14.12.2026 klo 14.00-15.00 suoritettavassa näytössä. Tarjouksien tulee olla sitovana voimassa, kunnes jonkun tarjouksen tehneen kanssa on allekirjoitettu sopimus, kuitenkin vähintään neljä (4) kuukautta tarjousten viimeisestä jättöpäivämäärästä lukien. Tilaaja ei korvaa urakkatarjouksen tekemisestä aiheutuvia kustannuksia tarjouksen tekijöille. Tarjouspyyntöön liittyviä tarkempia tietoja: Liite 1 Lähtökohtia Sallilan A-osan purkukilpailutukseen Liite 2 Sallilan koulun asemapiirustus Liite 3 Sallilan koulun pohjapiirustus, A-osa Liite 4 Sallilan koulun periaateleikkaus Liite 5 AHA, Sallilan koulu, Caverion Liite 6 Tiivistelmä Sallilan koulun kuntotutkimuksesta Kuvaus jatkuu kohdassa Hankintaa tai osaa koskevat lisätiedot.,
