title: 2026- Åpen tilbudskonkurranse - Leie og drift av sykehjemsplasser - Reservert for ideelle organisasjoner
description: Oppdragsgiver skal i tråd med politisk vedtak anskaffe 60-100 sykehjemsplasser for personer med demens og somatiske langtidsbehov.Det skal inngås leieavtale og tjenesteytingsavtale med en og samme leverandør. Det er en forutsetning for kontrakten at valgt leverandør fremskaffer, eier og stiller til disposisjon nødvendige lokaler på Askøy for tjenesteutførelsen. Leverandøren skal påta seg et totalansvar for å levere (utforme, prosjektere, bygge og leie ut), samt forvalte, drifte og vedlikeholde sykehjemmet.Konkurransen er reservert for ideelle organisasjoner, jf. anskaffelsesforskriften § 30-2a.Vi gjør oppmerksom på at det i kunngjøringsskjemaet er opplyst at det er en åpen anbudskonkurranse. Dette er fordi det per i dag ikke er teknisk mulig å velge prosedyren "åpen tilbudskonkurranse" i kunngjøringsskjemaet når skjema eForm 20 Helse- og sosialtjenester benyttes. Vi understreker imidlertid at prosedyren som skal benyttes er "åpen tilbudskonkurranse".

title: Åpenhet og inkludering - politiets samhandling med hele befolkningen
description: Formålet med forskningsoppdraget er å fremskaffe kunnskap om hvordan ulike grupper av befolkningen opplever politiet, hvilke forhold som påvirker samspillet mellom politi og innbyggere, og hvordan politiet kan sikre at ulike perspektiver og erfaringer blir hørt og ivaretatt. Det er behov for kunnskap om hvorvidt det er grupper som opplever at de ikke blir hørt, hvordan politiet når ut til grupper som i liten grad selv tar kontakt med politiet på eget initiativ og hvordan ulike former for kommunikasjon og dialog oppleves av ulike grupper. Forskningen skal gi et bedre kunnskapsgrunnlag for hvordan politiet kan styrke dialogen med befolkningen, tilpasse kommunikasjon og arbeidsformer til ulike målgrupper og utvikle tjenester som ivaretar rettssikkerhet, likebehandling og høy kvalitet. Forskningen skal også bidra med kunnskap om sammenheng mellom åpenhet, inkludering, tillit og politiets legitimitet, samt hvilken betydning dette kan ha for samfunnets motstandskraft. Se mer informasjon i konkurransegrunnlaget.

description: The Authority intends to establish a service for the provision of digital interpretation to support communication between staff and patients or service users of limited English proficiency across its acute and community sites. In the first instance, the Authority is procuring this service on a proportionate, time-limited basis for an initial term of 12 months, with an optional extension or extensions up to a further 12 months in duration, for a total of 24 months total maximum duration. The Authority seeks a suitably qualified supplier in order to evaluate service performance, user acceptance, information-governance assurance and value for money prior to any wider adoption and development of a HSE DSE Digital Interpretation Policy. The intended purpose of the service, in the main, is to support routine, low-acuity interactions, including: • patient registration, check-in and arrival at reception and outpatient departments; • wayfinding, directions and general enquiries; • appointment scheduling, confirmation and rescheduling; • general administrative exchanges of a comparable nature across acute, outpatient and community settings. • Collation of basic clinical detail and history An initial term of 12 months, with an optional extension or extensions up to a further 12 months in duration, for a total of 24 months total maximum duration.

title: Netherlands – Sanitary dispensing machines – Sanitaire voorzieningen
description: De gemeente Utrecht wil een Raamovereenkomst afsluiten met één Opdrachtnemer voor het leveren, plaatsen, onderhouden en verwijderen van kwalitatief hoogwaardige sanitaire voorzieningen tegen een optimale prijs-kwaliteitverhouding, die voldoen aan de gestelde eisen in het Programma van Eisen. De gemeente heeft getracht de kwaliteit en uitstraling van de huidige sanitaire voorzieningen daarin vast te leggen en ambieert dat de nieuw te leveren sanitaire voorzieningen minimaal gelijkwaardig zijn aan de huidige kwaliteit en uitstraling. Denk hierbij aan levensduur, degelijkheid, kleur en afmetingen. De opsomming is niet limitatief. Daarnaast bevat de nieuwe Raamovereenkomst een juiste borging van de dienstverlening, duidelijke communicatie, ontzorging en verduurzaming. De gemeente verwacht over de gehele looptijd (maximaal 8 jaar) van de Raamovereenkomst sanitaire voorzieningen af te nemen met een verwachte totale waarde van € 3.600.000,- (excl. BTW). Dit komt neer op een jaarlijkse verwachte waarde van € 450.000 per jaar (dit bedrag is inclusief de jaarlijkse indexatie en hierbeneden genoemde optie). Optie: afname extra hygiëneboxen (is bij start Raamovereenkomst geen onderdeel van de implementatieperiode) In de bovenstaande raming is rekening gehouden met de mogelijke uitrol tijdens de looptijd van Raamovereenkomst van extra circa 500 hygiëneboxen, wat een verwachte waarde heeft van circa € 54.000,- per jaar, nader gespecificeerd in het Programma van Eisen (bijlage 7) en Invulformulier tarieven (bijlage 9).

title: APN - NORAD Northern Basing Infrastructure (NNBI), Nunavut
description: Advance Procurement Notice NORAD Northern Basing Infrastructure (NNBI)  Forward Operating Location Iqaluit, Nunavut (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform Design-Builders of an upcoming contract opportunity at Forward Operating Location Iqaluit, Nunavut. The purpose of this APN is to allow Design-Builders to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested Design-Builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services The Department of National Defence (DND) is investing in infrastructure developments for the North American Aerospace Defence Command (NORAD) Modernization and Continental Defence at the Forward Operating Location Iqaluit, Nunavut.  This infrastructure investment aims to ensure that the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) have the tools they need to achieve their security and sovereignty objectives. These improvements will enable advanced aircraft operations and quick mobilization in the North for NORAD missions.   The infrastructure requirements for the FOL Iqaluit will include the following but are not limited to:  Airfield improvements;   Hangars with aprons and taxiways;   Ammunition compounds;  Fuel facilities;   Accommodations, warehousing, planning, multi-purpose facilities, and support equipment;   Robust IT, Cyber, and Logistics infrastructure.     Preliminary rough order of magnitude (ROM) estimates for the various facility components for each locations are as follows, subject to revision: Total hangar space, ~ 7,500 m2 Fuel storage, between 500,000 and 750,000 litres Office space  500 m2 Ammunition Storage 600 m2 Accommodations 4,000 m2 Fire Hall 2,000 m2 Multi-purpose facilities 9,000 m2 Indoor storage (Total), 7,000 m2 Apron 60,000 m2 Total asphalt surface 72,000 m2 The delivery method for this infrastructure will be a Modified Design-Build (MDB) contract, with one MDB contract for the site and an estimated total contract value that may exceed $5B. This multi-year contract consists of the following sequential and/or concurrent phases and are not limited to:  Requirements validation, concept development, market analysis and planning activities.   Design Phase activities.  Construction Phase activities.   It is anticipated that the Request for Proposal (RFP) will include detailed evaluation criteria; however, these remain subject to change and will be finalized and fully described in the RFP documentation upon release. At a high level, it is expected that the RFP will assess proponents on demonstrated experience across a range of factors, including northern design and construction experience, experience delivering similar asset types (both within and outside of northern environments), and the integration of design and construction capabilities within a single team. Key personnel requirements will include demonstrated northern experience for certain roles. The evaluation of approach and methodology is expected to consider how proponents plan to successfully deliver projects in northern environments, including logistics, climate, and constructability considerations, as well as their approach to Indigenous participation based on principles of meaningful participation and mitigation of potential adverse effects. In addition to the technical evaluation, a formal interview process will be conducted to further assess team capability to successfully deliver the project in a northern environment. The terms and conditions of the contract will allow for self-performed work by the design-build team.    The MDB solicitation for Iqaluit is projected to be released in Fall 2027. This is conditional on receiving approval to proceed by DND.   The Government of Canada is committed to advancing reconciliation and fostering meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples. In support of these commitments, DND aims to create opportunities for Indigenous businesses and communities through meaningful subcontracting, employment, and training related to the proposed project.  To align with these objectives, the successful proponents will be required to develop an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP) as part of the MDB contract. The IBP will outline proposed initiatives and opportunities for Indigenous participation, including subcontracting, employment, and training activities.  Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a Design-Builder will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Facility Security Clearance at the level of SECRET. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing Design-Builders early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, Design-Builders that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, design-builders are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 87007; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the Design-Builders to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a Design-Builder: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has  met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal DCC will  send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. title: ITS4US Deployment Accelerator
description: The Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) Joint Program Office (JPO) looks to accelerate the replication of innovative technology solutions developed by large-scale deployment projects that it sponsors. ITS JPO believes that successful demonstration of these solutions by multiple agencies validates the technology's maturity and readiness for broader implementation across the industry. The purpose of this Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) is to award up to five (5) operational pilots that will test integrated technology solutions developed and deployed by the ITS4US Deployment Program. Each awardee will develop, test, and deploy solutions modeled on ITS4US deployment project documentation and its associated open-source software. In addition, the awardees will form a deployer cohort where they receive USDOT-funded technical support designed to accelerate implementation. Awardees can build faster, better, and cheaper by launching related efforts together, and use the insight of peers who have recently succeeded in addressing similar challenges. See Attachments for further information.

description: July 7, 2026: This is Amendment 0009 to solicitation 47QRCA23R0001 The General Services Administration (GSA), Federal Acquisition Service (FAS), Office of Acquisition Solutions Development (ASD), is issuing Amendment 0009 in accordance with RFO-2025-05 Supplement 1 FAR 5.101 for the One Acquisition Solution for Integrated Services Plus (OASIS+), Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ), Multi-Agency Contracts (MAC). The System for Award Management (SAM.gov) is the official source for information about this procurement. Should GSA determine a need to close any domain or solicitation, the agency will provide public notification. Offerors are permitted to submit a single proposal for multiple domains under a single solicitation. There is no fixed timeline for award; timelines will vary based on the volume of proposals received and are subject to resource availability. Offerors must be registered and active in SAM.gov. All proposals must be submitted through the OASIS+ SubmissionPortal (OSP). The OSP is open for registration and submission of offers as of January 12, 2026. Registration information and submission instructions are provided at https://oasis.app.cloud.gov/. For questions related to registration or technical issues, offerors can contact client.support@apexlogic.com. Industry is instructed to review the solicitation requirements and all amendments before submitting an offer. Offerors submitting a new offer after issuance of Amendment 0009 must acknowledge all current amendments in the OSP by completing the required amendment acknowledgement action during offer submission. A signed SF 33 remains required as part of all offer submissions; however, a separate signed SF30 upload is not required for new offers submitted after issuance of Amendment 0009 unless otherwise directed by the Government. Offerors that submitted an offer prior to issuance of Amendment 0009 and who have not received a contract award or unsuccessful notice are required to acknowledge Amendment 0009 by signing this SF 30 and uploading the signed SF 30 in Symphony to the Business Factors section for the applicable RFP no later than July 15, 2026. Offerors with pending offers under more than one OASIS+ RFP must upload the signed SF30 to the Business Factors section of each applicable RFP for which acknowledgement is required. Offerors are responsible for ensuring that the signed SF30 uploaded for each pending offer corresponds to the correct OASIS+ RFP. Please follow the steps below to upload the signed SF 30 in Symphony: Login to Symphony at https://oasis.app.cloud.gov/. Navigate to My Company. Navigate to the Business Factors page. Ensure the "My Solicitation Preferences" field is set to any OASIS+ solicitation to display the appropriate factors. Scroll down to the Other Documents section to see the Amendment 9 SF30 factor for each solicitation. Click the Amendment 9 factor for solicitations submitted prior to Amendment 9 release (Example: "Amendment 9 SF30 - OASIS+ 8(a) Continuously Open"). Upload the signed SF30 document and select the checkbox to certify the claim for the factor. Click "Save and Claim" for the factor. The signed SF30 is required for amendment acknowledgement purposes only. Offerors shall not submit revised proposal documents, additional supporting documentation, or other proposal changes. Failure to submit the signed SF30 by the stated deadline may result in the offer being ineligible for further consideration. Offerors are solely responsible for reviewing and staying current with the solicitation and all amendments posted on SAM.gov. In the event of a conflict, the solicitation and amendments posted to this notice on SAM.gov take precedence over any information contained on other websites or prior communications. title: Multi Mission Surface Combatant (MMSC) Post Delivery Execution Yard (PDEY)
description: PAE Maritime Solicitation N61177-27-R-0003 for the execution of post-delivery availabilities on four (4) Multi Mission Surface Combatants (MMSC) during a 14-month Post Delivery (PD) period for each ship. To effectively and efficiently accomplish necessary industrial work, three availabilities are planned for each ship in the MMSC post-delivery schedule. At a minimum, this includes a Post Shakedown Availability (PSA) following MMSC transit from Marinette, Wisconsin and prior to Post Delivery Test & Trials (PDT&T), an Industrial Post Delivery Availability (IPDA) following PDT&T, and a Continuous Maintenance Availability (CMAV) at the conclusion of the post-delivery period. Also, concurrent Planned Maintenance Availabilities (PMAVs) may be tasked to the shipyard during these scheduled industrial availabilities. These availabilities will be accomplished under the Post Delivery Execution Yard (PDEY) Contract. Cost Plus Award Fee (CPAF) task orders will be issued to support Post Delivery work for MMSC 1-4. The PD Execution Yard Contractor responsibilities include: 1. Preparation and Management of PSA, IPDA, and CMAV 2. Drydocking of MMSC during PSA 3. Execution of PSA, IPDA, and CMAV as well as concurrent PMAVs 4. Post Repair Trials (PRT) at the conclusion of PSA 5. Emergent Work identified prior to or during the PSA 6. Providing test, trials, readiness, and inspection support for the PSA The Period of Performance of the contract is intended to cover the Post Delivery periods for all 4 MMSCs. See PIEE link for Solicitation and related attachments: https://piee.eb.mil/sol/xhtml/unauth/search/oppMgmtLink.xhtml?noticeId=N6117727R0003&noticeType=SolicitationNotice

title: Netherlands – Road transport services – Besloten Buspendeldienst TESO veerhaven Texel– Joost Dourleinkazerne V.V.
description: Het doel van de Aanbestedende dienst is het sluiten van een Raamovereenkomst met één Opdrachtnemer voor de verzorging van een Besloten Buspendeldienst. De Raamovereenkomst wordt gesloten voor een periode van 4 jaar waarbij na de eerste twee (2) jaar de mogelijkheid bestaat om de Overeenkomst eenzijdig op te zeggen. De opdracht omvat het vervoeren van medewerkers van het Ministerie van Defensie vanaf TESO veerhaven Texel naar de Joost Dourleinkazerne te Texel en vice versa, van maandag t/m vrijdag, exclusief feestdagen, op vaste tijden. De Aanbestedende dienst wil op werkdagen, exclusief feestdagen, gebruik maken van de dienstverlening. Het gaat om dagelijks 2 ritten van TESO veerhaven Texel naar Joost Dourleinkazerne te Texel en vice versa. Op de eerste woensdag van de maand gaat het om een extra rit. title: Pre-solicitation Notice: On-Ramp for the Department of Defense OMNIBUS IV Multiple-Award Contract
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice to synopsize the intention of the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) for an on-ramp to the OMNIBUS IV Multiple Award, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract vehicle covering military medical research and development services. The eventual RFP will be set-aside for small businesses certified under the Small Business Administration 8(a) Program. The Government anticipates making multiple new awards under this on-ramp, and all new awards will align with the existing unrestricted contract vehicle. This notice is not a request for proposals and does not commit the Government to any contractual agreement. The OMNIBUS IV contract vehicle was awarded under full and open competition with a base ordering period of 20 June 2022 through 19 June 2027 and an Option Ordering Period of 20 June 2027 ? 19 June 2032. Task orders may be competed under fair opportunity (providing all Contract Holders within a Market Segment the opportunity to submit a proposal) or an exception to fair opportunity (such as set-asides for small businesses or applicable small business socioeconomic categories). The cumulative ceiling of this unrestricted IDIQ contract vehicle is $10 billion. To date, the accumulated awarded task order value (including future unexercised option periods) is over $600 million across 51 task orders. Task Orders have been issued by a growing number of end users including DHACA, the U.S. Army Medical Research Acquisition Activity (now integrated into DHACA), the Naval Supply Systems Command, and the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences. When excluding the task orders simply providing a minimum guarantee to the existing Contract Holders, 51 task orders have been issued off this contract vehicle with 8 task orders being set aside for the 8(a) Program and 9 task orders being awarded to an 8(a) Participant. 33 task orders have been awarded so far to small businesses under this contract vehicle. Of the 51 task orders, 94% were awarded during the Government Fiscal Years 2024 - 2026, and the amount of competitive task orders has grown each fiscal year. The Government anticipates releasing the formal RFP for the OMNIBUS IV on-ramp on SAM.gov around late January 2026 (at least 15 calendar days from the posting of this notice. Please see attachments for further details.

title: 417 SCMS Landing Gear Depot Support (LGDS)
description: 417th SCMS Landing Gear Depot Support (LGDS) Request for Information This announcement constitutes an official Request for Information (RFI). This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an Invitation for Bid (IFB), nor is it to be construed as a commitment by the government. The Government will not pay for any information provided in response to this RFI. Scope The 417th Landing Gear Supply Chain Management Squadron (417 SCMS), Enterprise Hill Commodity Council (EHCC) and Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) are developing a strategy to support Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) Depot production goals associated with the B-52, C-5, C-130, KC-135, and E-3 platforms. This strategy will subsume the workload currently supported under the Landing Gear Performance Based Logistics (LG-PBL1) contract, while expanding support to the B-52 and C-5 platforms. The primary goals of this future contract are to provide: 1.) Complete Component Parts Kits: Support Depot remanufacture of landing gear Depot Level Reparables (DLRs) for all five weapon systems, 2.) Remanufacture Support: Fulfill remanufacturing requirements based on the delta between supply chain need and depot production capability. 3.) Process Offload: Relieve operational bottlenecks and single-point process failures (e.g. plating, grinding) at the organic depot. Background The 417 SCMS currently supports the LGDS requirements through multiple vehicles: LG-PBL1 Contract: Single-award, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) award-term contract (consisting of a 5-year base and two 5-year award terms), supporting the C-130, E-3, and KC-135, expiring in 2032. The prime contractor is responsible for the quality and delivery of all parts. This contract operates under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP), incorporating a direct sales approach with incentives/disincentives tied to outcome-based performance metrics. Remanufacture percentages are roughly 60% organic Depot, and 40% contractor facility. Organic Depot Support: The B-52 and C-5 are remanufactured 100% organically at the OO-ALC depot, with individual component parts (kit parts) purchased transactionally through DLA. Developing Strategy The USAF owns the preponderance of the technical data and maintains a Boeing Rights Guard agreement for limited data on the E-3 and KC-135 landing gear systems. The Government has determined that to be successful this contract strategy must: Allow the contractor to leverage the Government�s buying power for consumable parts, while streamlining and improving the purchase process. Provide a single contractor with management responsibility for the entire population of replacement parts supporting DLRs. Improve forecasting and inventory accuracy Provide relief for single-point process bottlenecks (e.g., plating, grinding) within the organic depot Provide remanufacture support for all DLRs beyond the throughput capacity of Government depot, to be fulfilled at the prime contractor�s facility. Incorporate properly balanced incentives and disincentives for contractor performance Due to the nature of this effort, the complexity and magnitude of the transition process, and the need for a single point of accountability, the Government intends to award a 15-year IDIQ-type contract. The single-award long-term approach will allow the contractor ample time to conduct the necessary research for proper phase-in of consumable kits, and support the transition of current LG-PBL1 workload. The Government intends to develop an outcome-based support contract utilizing a workshare payment approach. The primary objectives of this contract are to: (1) Improve landing gear piece part and assembly supportability (2) Provide remanufacture support beyond organic capacity 4.0 Performance Expectations Performance requirements under the future contract will include: Asset Availability of consumable kits to support OO-ALC Depot production lines Core remanufacture support for E-3, KC-135, and C-130. Potential expanded remanufacture support for B-52 and/or C-5. Industrial process (e.g. plating, grinding,) offload at the contractor�s facility when organic depot bottlenecking occurs. The LGDS acquisition team is asking for feedback from Industry representatives regarding this strategic support acquisition for Landing Gear spare parts. 5.0 Industry Feedback Questions: Please provide the following business information for your company:: Company Name Address Point of Contact CAGE Code Phone Number E-mail Address Web Page URL Size of Business under NAICS Code 336413 (Small Business Size Standard is 1,250 employees) The Government is anticipating a 15-year Firm-Fixed-Price contract for this effort. Describe any commercial risks, pricing volatility, or supply chain issues your company foresees with a 15-year duration. What Economic Price Adjustment (EPA) indices (e.g., specific Bureau of Labor Statistics PPI codes) or adjustment mechanisms would you recommend to mitigate long-term pricing risk? Describe your company's capability to procure all parts listed in Attachment 1 (Consumable Kits). What predictive tools, supply chain modeling, or consumption tracking methods do you use to anticipate demand and mitigate long-lead consumable shortages (e.g., specialized fasteners, seals, forgings)? What experience do you have supporting variable/operationally dependent Air Force parts needs, including surge requirements? Describe your company�s in-house capability and annual capacity to remanufacture the parts listed in Attachment 2 (LG-PBL1 NIINs). Does your company have experience providing parts and production support for complex landing gear assemblies throughout the remanufacture process? Please describe your company�s experience with USAF/Landing Gear engineering protocols, Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs), and Quality Management. Describe your company�s experience managing legacy USAF weapon system component obsolescence and resolving recurring non-conforming parts issues within a remanufacturing environment. Does your company have the capability and experience to train, qualify, and certify personnel to perform critical military-grade remanufacturing processes? Describe your experience providing transition support from an expiring government contract to a new government contract. Describe your experience integrating with and using Government software systems. 6.0 Submission Instructions The Government is accepting responses to this request for information via email only. Please provide written responses to the Contracting Officers and Program Manager by 11 January 2027 at the following email addresses: Nathan Flinders Contracting Officer Nathan.flinders@dla.mil Justin Rogers Contracting Officer Justin.rogers.28@us.af.mil Trevor Russell Program Manager Trevor.Russell.2@us.af.mil Attachments: Consumable Kits List by WS Current LG-PBL1 NIINs

title: Defense Innovation Unit Commercial Solutions Opening
description: The Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) is interested in awarding funding agreements (Agreements) to nontraditional and traditional defense contractors to carry out prototype projects that are directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of military personnel and the supporting platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense (DoD), or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the Armed Forces of the United States. As such, DIU hereby announces the release of their streamlined Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). This CSO is seeking proposals for innovative, commercial technologies that accelerate attainment of asymmetric defense capabilities. In this context, innovative means any new technology, process, or business practice, or any new application of an existing technology, process, or business practice that contributes to the sustainment of global peace and U.S. national security. Agreements will be sought under an open (available for five (5) years), competitive (solution brief/demonstration followed by proposal) CSO. This CSO is considered a competitive process, intended to ensure that competitive procedures are used to the maximum extent practicable when entering into Agreements to carry out these prototype projects. Interested parties with current or new/developmental innovative technological solutions or enhancements are highly encouraged to visit the DIU website to obtain more information regarding the process of presenting their solutions to DIU and the potential for securing said Agreements under this CSO. Topic Areas of Interest (AoI) will be posted on the DIU website and may be updated at any time. Please note that the submission period for solution briefs under the identified AOI's will be open for a limited period of time, so check the DIU website for updates frequently. DIU's website is: https://www.diu.mil/work-with-us

title: Netherlands – Repair and maintenance services – Heraanbesteding Vervanging Verlichting Centrum-Parkeergarage Etten-Leur
description: De gemeente Etten-Leur heeft in het centrum van Etten-Leur een ondergrondse parkeergarage met een capaciteit van 1000 parkeerplaatsen. De gemeente is voornemens de bestaande verlichting te vervangen door LED-verlichting, deze deels uit te breiden waar nodig en een bijbehorend meerjarig onderhoudsplan te laten opstellen. Gedurende de uitvoering van de werkzaamheden zal de parkeergarage in gebruik blijven. Het is dus belangrijk dat veiligheid en overlast zoveel mogelijk beperkt blijft. Met de toepassing van LED-armaturen levert de gemeente een bijdrage aan de te bereiken doelstellingen op het gebied van energiebesparing. Ook geeft deze vervanging meer zichtbaarheid in de parkeergarage. De werkzaamheden bestaan in hoofdzaak uit: - Het leveren en vervangen van alle bestaande armaturen door LED-verlichting; - Het uitbreiden van de bestaande verlichtingsinstallatie volgens bijgevoegd verlichtingsplan; - Het installeren van een bedieningsinstallatie/paneel; - Het bedrijfsklaar opleveren van de verlichtingsinstallatie; - Het aanleveren van revisiegegevens; - Het opstellen van een meerjarig onderhoudsplan (15 jaar) t.b.v de LED-verlichting. Voor de uitvoering dient van de bestaande infrastructuur te worden uitgegaan. Uitzondering hierop is de uitbreiding van de bestaande verlichtingsinstallatie volgens verlichtingsplan. De volgende hoeveelheden zijn van toepassing: Conform het Prijzenblad met hoeveelheden (Bijlage a) gaat het om het leveren en installeren van in totaal 1310 stuks armaturen.

buyer: Inspection fédérale de la sécurité nucléaire IFSN
title: Switzerland – Data services – (26163) 998 Technikpartner WEB
description: L'Inspection fédérale de la sécurité nucléaire (IFSN) est tenue de fournir des informations au public et aux autorités. Le site web de l'IFSN met à la disposition du public toutes les informations pertinentes et comprend une rubrique « Actualités » ainsi que des contenus statiques tels que des pages, des documents et le Forum technique. Le site web respecte les directives de la Confédération en matière d’identité visuelle (CI) et de conception (CD) et est multilingue (allemand, français, italien et anglais). Des contenus sont également disponibles en « langue simplifiée » et en « langue des signes ». L’IFSN exploite les trois sites web ENSI, ENSI-RAT et EGT-Suisse sur une base technique uniforme avec une configuration WordPress multisite, un design cohérent, des plugins spécifiques à l’IFSN et des interfaces vers des systèmes externes. L’infrastructure d’hébergement, dotée de différents environnements de développement, garantit un fonctionnement sécurisé. L’appel d’offres a pour objectif le changement de partenaire technique et d’hébergement, ainsi que la mise en place d’un « darksite » autonome pouvant être activé en cas d’urgence ou de crise. Nous recherchons un partenaire technique chargé de l’exploitation sécurisée, de la maintenance et du développement de l’infrastructure technique. Cela comprend la gestion des sites web existants, la migration vers un partenaire d’hébergement adapté, ainsi que la gestion de projet et la mise en œuvre du « darksite ».

Als akademisches Lehrkrankenhaus des Universitäts-klinikums Hamburg-Eppendorf (UKE) ist es mit derzeit 527 Planbetten im Krankenhausbedarfsplan des Landes Niedersachsen ausgewiesen. Als solches beherbergt es die Entbindungsstation mit sieben Kreißsälen.
